records.finding: `sized = true` is set before the history and observed queries run, so a flow WITH a baseline whose lookback window holds no entry-stage history (hist is empty, the currency loop runs zero times) leaves the leg Unavailable=false with empty Low/Mid/High maps and no note explaining them; Summary then prints `unrealized [estimate] none` (engine/report/summary.go:68) beside the new note `nothing is credited back; this is gross suppressed demand`. That contradicts ADR-0020 line 32-33 and the decision shard (`marked Unavailable whenever no requested flow could be sized`) and portability invariant 6.3 (ungrounded MUST be a structural marker, never a plausible zero). Setting sized only after a currency actually contributed a range (or marking Unavailable when hist is empty, with a note) closes it.
records.evidence: engine/unrealized.go:106 `sized = true` precedes `hist, err := hourlyEntriesByCurrency(...)`; probe run over engine.Unrealized with `baseline: { seasonality: hour_of_week, lookback_weeks: 1 }` and zero metric points: `Unavailable=false low=map[] mid=map[] high=map[] notes=["flow \"invoice.pay\" declares no recovery model — nothing is credited back; this is gross suppressed demand (ADR-0020)"]`; ADR-0020:32 `The leg is now marked `Unavailable` whenever no requested flow could be sized`
records.reason: CONFIRMED by the cross-examiner in round 1: Reproduced at HEAD (round probe, three zero-history variants): Unavailable=false, Low/Mid/High all empty, the only note the new 'declares no recovery model' line. The same probe against a git-archive copy of base 1a6da9d (with the then-required recovery/reconcile blocks added) gives Unavailable=false, empty maps and NO notes — so the raw behaviour (baseline present, zero history -> empty maps, Unavailable=false) is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here. It is nevertheless this range's defect: the ADR (docs/adr/0020 lines 31-33) and the shard's `decided` text assert 'the leg is now marked Unavailable whenever no requested flow could be sized, which it was not before (it returned empty maps a renderer could print as zero)', and the mechanism the range adds to deliver that sentence — the `sized` flag — is set at line 106 before either query, so it records 'reached the query step', not 'was sized'. A flow whose lookback window is empty returns exactly the empty maps the ADR parenthetical names as the closed defect. The renderer consequence holds: Summary prints `unrealized [estimate] none`, and `money()`/`moneyRange()` render 'none' for an empty realized map too, where it means a measured zero — so 'none' on the unrealized line reads as a measured zero with no structural marker and no note naming why, which is what invariant 6.3 forbids. The scenario is realistic (a service younger than its lookback, e.g. the quickstart adopter adding a baseline on day one; a querier with undeclared MetricHistoryWeeks takes the non-gap path). The code comment's own definition ('reached the estimate') does not rescue the ADR's stronger, verbatim claim. Severity stands as filed. — fixed in 6348fde (round-1 repair).

records.finding: The contract (and ADR-0020:29, registry/registry.go:325) says a present block, empty included, is validated in full and only an absent block is accepted — but a present key with a null value (`baseline:` with no body, `baseline: ~`, `baseline: null`) decodes to a nil pointer in the reference implementation and loads as absent (`shortfall validate` exits 0 for all three). The contract says nothing about the null form and no vector pins it, so a port whose YAML library yields an empty mapping for null rejects under `baseline_seasonality` what the reference accepts, breaking the section's own `MUST validate it identically`; it is also the shape a commented-out block body leaves behind, silently turning a typo into `no baseline`.
records.evidence: docs/portability/registry.md:32 `a present block — empty included — is validated in full under the classes of 4.3`; fixture `    baseline:` (null) -> `ok — 1 flow(s), 1 segment(s)`; registry/registry.go:332 `Baseline  *baselineDoc  `yaml:"baseline,omitempty"`` with no null check before `if fd.Baseline != nil`
records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner in round 1: The observation is accurate but the accuracy claim is not. Verified at HEAD with `go run ./cmd/shortfall validate`: `baseline:` (bare), `baseline: ~`, `baseline: null` and `reconcile:` all load (exit 0); `baseline: {}`, `recovery: {}` and `reconcile: { source: "   " }` are rejected. yaml.v3 decodes a null scalar into a pointer field by setting the pointer to nil (decoder.null: Interface/Ptr/Map/Slice get their zero value), so a null-valued key is indistinguishable from an omitted key at the doc level — the reference treats it as absent by construction, not by oversight. The contract sentence as written is not false for that form: 'a present block — empty included' names a mapping (`{}` is the empty one, and the ADR's own words are 'an empty block is a typo'); a null value is no mapping at all, so the sentence is silent on null rather than wrong about it. The failure scenario requires 'a port whose YAML library yields an empty mapping for null'; no mainstream decoder does (PyYAML -> None, js-yaml/SnakeYAML -> null, serde_yaml Option -> None, yaml.v3 pointer -> nil), and a port decoding into a value-typed struct cannot distinguish absent from present at all, so it cannot implement the contract's absent/present split in the first place — the divergent port is hypothetical. The identical unpinned pattern pre-exists in this same section for `estimator`, an omitempty pointer since base: at HEAD `estimator:` (null) loads and `estimator: {}` is rejected under estimator_default_minor, and the contract has never mentioned the null form for it. The commented-out-body case (`baseline:` followed only by `#` lines) does load as absent — verified — but whether YAML's own null idiom should count as 'present' is a design question ADR-0020 answered ('the way to declare no block is to omit it'; `{}` is the typo marker), not a false statement in the contract; pinning a `null_block` accept vector would be a non-blocking follow-up. Note that at base the null form WAS rejected (value-typed struct left zero-valued -> baseline_seasonality), so the range does newly admit it — the same way it newly admits omission, which is the decision.

records.finding: The regenerated `minimal` facts encode an absent block as a zero-valued sub-object (`seasonality: ""`, `lookback_weeks: 0`, `model: ""`, `source: ""`) — values the `baseline_lookback`/`recovery_model`/`reconcile_source_required` classes reject when declared — and no contract text says an absent block yields zero-valued facts rather than an omitted or null block. Before this diff every accepted vector carried all three, so the facts shape for absence is newly unspecified; a port serializing absence as null fails the checklist's `yields the committed facts` step without the contract saying who is wrong.
records.evidence: testkit/vectors/registry.json:104-107 `"baseline": { "seasonality": "", "lookback_weeks": 0 }`; docs/portability/checklist.md:38 `every `accept` vector loads and yields the committed facts`; testkit/vectors.go:349-359 copies flow.Baseline/Recovery/Reconcile unconditionally
records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner in round 1: The committed vector is itself the contract's answer to 'who is wrong'. testkit/vectors.go (untouched in this range — not in the stat) defines the facts JSON schema as 'the observable output of validation', states that every expected value 'is produced by running the reference implementation', and documents in the `Equal` comment exactly how each field renders: non-omitempty fields (which BaselineFact/RecoveryFact/ReconcileFact are, as value-typed `json:"baseline"` etc.) render in full, while only the omitempty pointer `estimator` is dropped when absent, pinned by TestRegistryFactsEqualNilVersusEmpty. Equal compares over that JSON rendering, so the `minimal` vector's `"baseline": {"seasonality": "", "lookback_weeks": 0}` is a fully determined pin, and a port emitting `null` or omitting the key is wrong by the checklist's own step ('yields the committed facts') — that is the contract saying who is wrong, in its executable half. The zero-valued form is also unambiguous: no valid document can produce a present baseline with `seasonality: ""` or a present recovery with `model: ""` or a present reconcile with `source: ""` (each is rejected — verified by the empty-block fixtures and the reject vectors), so 'absent' is the only document that yields those facts and nothing collapses into it; the estimator comment's 'no estimator vs estimator of zero must not collapse' concern does not arise here. That the three blocks use value-typed facts while estimator uses a pointer is a pre-existing schema choice (FlowFact shape unchanged since base); changing it would be a VectorsVersion bump and is a design follow-up at most, not a defect of this range. The 'newly unspecified' claim fails: the shape was specified by the same code and comments before the diff, and the regenerated vector merely exercises it.

records.reason: CONFIRMED by the cross-examiner in round 3: engine/unrealized.go:42 at head: `leg.Notes = []string{"unavailable: the counterfactual leg needs a registry (baseline lookback, stages, recovery)"}` -- unchanged by the diff (present verbatim at base). Its truth changed in this range: at base the registry validator required a recovery block on every flow, so recovery was in fact a precondition of the leg; head's registry.go:646 validates recovery only when present, ADR-0020 Decision says 'No recovery: the estimate is gross, and the note says so', and this range's own :190-199 path sizes the leg without one and emits the gross-demand note (TestUnrealizedAbsentBlocks 'no recovery: sized gross' passes at head). So the user-facing note now names a requirement the leg no longer has, while the sibling absent-baseline note at :81-86 was rewritten to ADR-0020 wording in the same range. Baseline lookback and stages remain genuine requirements; only 'recovery' is stale. A LOW wording drift, severity as filed (unmapped). — fixed in the round-3 repair commit, at the cap; scoped re-review in round 4.

records.finding: ADR-0020 says ports 'MUST still reject a present, empty block under the existing classes' and the portability doc says the empty `{}` mapping is validated in full, but the accept side gained two vectors (`minimal`, `null_blocks`) while no rejection vector carries `baseline: {}`, `recovery: {}` or `reconcile: {}`. The nearest, `reconcile_source_required`, mutates `source: ""` inside a non-empty mapping, so a port that treats an empty mapping as an absent block — the very confusion the ADR warns about — passes every vector; only registry_test.go (Go-only) pins it.
records.evidence: {"reconcile_source_required", "a present reconcile block must name its ledger; the way to declare none is to omit the block (ADR-0020)", "reconcile_source_required", sub(`source: "sql:ledger.payments"`, `source: ""`)}  — vs ADR-0020 Consequences: "Ports MUST accept the minimal document and MUST still reject a present, empty block under the existing classes."
records.reason: CONFIRMED by the cross-examiner in round 3: Judged against both texts. (a) Class or instance: a present-empty block is NOT a new rejection class. Probe (round-hdk5v1/probe2/main.go) at head: `baseline: {}` -> 'baseline seasonality "" is not supported' (class baseline_seasonality), `recovery: {}` -> 'recovery model "" is not supported' (recovery_model), `reconcile: {}` -> 'reconcile block names no source' (reconcile_source_required); ADR-0020 says exactly this ('under the existing classes'). So 4.3's letter -- 'every class has at least one vector ... differing from the reference document by exactly one edit' -- is satisfied; the candidate does not show a class without a vector. (b) The gap is nonetheless real and new in this range: testkit/vectors/registry.json at head contains no `{}` for any of the three blocks (grep finds only the pre-existing `flows: {}` in no_flows); every baseline_*/recovery_*/reconcile_* vector mutates a field inside a non-empty mapping, so a port that collapses an empty mapping to an absent block -- the empty-vs-absent distinction this range creates; at base both were rejected, so no port could confuse them -- passes all 79 vectors and the checklist.md 38-40 conformance steps while violating ADR-0020's new Consequences MUST ('MUST still reject a present, empty block') and the new 4.1 sentence ('A present mapping -- the empty {} included -- is validated in full'). Only registry_test.go TestOptionalFlowBlocks (Go-only, added in this range) pins it. The repo's own convention pins such shapes under an existing class: recovery_fraction_nan is a second vector for class recovery_fraction, and 4.3 says 'The recovery_fraction_nan vector pins this'; a `baseline: {}` (or `reconcile: {}`) vector is a one-edit mutation of the reference and fits that pattern. The accept half of the same ADR sentence got minimal and null_blocks; the reject half got nothing. Confirmed as the LOW gap filed, with the clarification that the remedy is an additional vector under an existing class, not a new class in the 4.3 table. — fixed in the round-3 repair commit, at the cap; scoped re-review in round 4.
